entities.name: Oral Torah (Torah she-be'al peh)
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The foundational rabbinic concept that God revealed two Torahs at Sinai: the Written Torah (the Pentateuch) and the Oral Torah — interpretive traditions, legal rulings, and commentaries transmitted orally from Moses through the prophets, elders, and sages to the rabbis. This doctrine legitimizes rabbinic authority to interpret and expand biblical law, creating a dynamic legal system (halakha) capable of adaptation to new circumstances. Initially forbidden to be written down, the Oral Torah was eventually codified in the Mishnah (c. 200 CE) and Talmud (c. 500 CE) due to existential threats to its oral transmission. The concept of "dual Torah" is what distinguishes Rabbinic Judaism from other forms of ancient Judaism.
